chapters.title: Chapter 1: Anatomy and Physiology of the Hypothalamic–Pituitary Axis and Water Homeostasis
chapters.description: Covers the structural and functional organization of the hypothalamus and posterior pituitary with emphasis on osmoregulation, synthesis and release of antidiuretic hormone (ADH/vasopressin), and the renal mechanisms of water handling.
subtopics: Anatomy of the hypothalamus, supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei, and posterior pituitary
Synthesis, storage and secretion of vasopressin (ADH)
Osmoreceptors and baroreceptors regulating ADH release
Renal water reabsorption: V2 receptors, aquaporins and collecting duct physiology
Interaction between renal sodium handling and water balance
Physiologic responses to hypovolemia, hyperosmolality and stress

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Classification of Hyponatraemia
chapters.description: Explains the mechanisms that cause hyponatraemia, the classification by tonicity and volume status, the diagnostic algorithm, and common causes including SIADH.
subtopics: Definition and classification: hypotonic, isotonic, hypertonic hyponatraemia
Assessment of volume status and its clinical limitations
Primary mechanisms: excess water intake, impaired free water excretion, sodium loss
Diagnostic workup: serum osmolality, urine osmolality, urine sodium, plasma and urine electrolytes
Differential diagnosis framework: hypovolaemic, euvolaemic, hypervolaemic hyponatraemia
Common etiologies with focus on SIADH: CNS disorders, pulmonary disease, drugs, malignancy

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH)
chapters.description: Detailed overview of SIADH pathogenesis, diagnostic criteria, laboratory features, clinical manifestations, and complications.
subtopics: Diagnostic criteria for SIADH (euvolaemic hypotonic hyponatraemia with inappropriately concentrated urine)
Mechanisms of inappropriate ADH secretion: ectopic production, central stimulation, drug-induced
Laboratory profile: low serum osmolality, high urine osmolality, elevated urine sodium, ADH levels
Clinical manifestations across severity: nausea, headache, hiccups, confusion, seizures
Complications: cerebral oedema, rhabdomyolysis, risks of rapid correction
Causes of SIADH related to CNS inflammation and malignancy

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Fluid and Electrolyte Management Strategies in Hyponatraemia
chapters.description: Principles of treating hyponatraemia including acute versus chronic management, methods for safe sodium correction, and specific therapeutics (fluid restriction, hypertonic saline, demeclocycline, vaptans).
subtopics: Initial assessment and safety priorities in severe symptomatic hyponatraemia
Fluid restriction rationale and practical implementation
Use of hypertonic saline: indications, dosing, monitoring and calculation of sodium change
Vasopressin receptor antagonists (tolvaptan, conivaptan): mechanism, indications and precautions
Other pharmacologic options: demeclocycline, urea
Prevention and management of osmotic demyelination syndrome: recommended correction limits and monitoring

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Behçet's Disease — Epidemiology, Clinical Features and Diagnostic Criteria
chapters.description: Foundational knowledge on Behçet's disease (BD): incidence and demographic patterns, cardinal clinical manifestations across organ systems, and established diagnostic/classification criteria.
subtopics: Epidemiology and geographic distribution; genetic and environmental risk factors
Classic triad: recurrent oral aphthous ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis
Mucocutaneous manifestations: folliculitis-like lesions, erythema nodosum, pathergy phenomenon
Systemic involvement: ocular, vascular, gastrointestinal, articular, neurological
International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease (ICBD) and other diagnostic frameworks
Features that suggest severe or organ-threatening disease

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Immunopathogenesis and Genetics of Behçet's Disease
chapters.description: Describes the immune mechanisms implicated in BD, the role of innate and adaptive immunity, cytokine networks, and genetic associations such as HLA-B51.
subtopics: Role of neutrophil hyperactivity and endothelial dysfunction
Key cytokines and mediators: IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α, interferon pathways
Monocyte activation and inflammatory cascades relevant to systemic and CNS disease
Genetic associations: HLA-B51 and non-HLA loci
Implications of immunopathogenesis for targeted therapies

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Neuro-Behçet's Disease — Clinical Presentations, Pathology and Prognosis
chapters.description: Covers neurological involvement in BD: types of presentations (parenchymal and non-parenchymal), typical lesion locations, CSF findings, natural history and prognostic factors.
subtopics: Classification: parenchymal vs non-parenchymal (venous thrombosis) neuro-BD
Common clinical syndromes: meningoencephalitis, brainstem syndromes, cognitive/psychiatric manifestations
Typical lesion distribution: brainstem, basal ganglia, thalamus, hemispheric white matter
CSF features: lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, opening pressure changes
Disease course: acute, relapsing and chronic progressive patterns
Prognostic indicators and long-term outcomes

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Neuroimaging and its Limitations in Neuroinflammatory Diseases
chapters.description: Principles of MRI and other neuroimaging modalities used to detect neuroinflammation, typical imaging patterns in neuro-BD and reasons why imaging can be normal in early or mild disease.
subtopics: MRI sequences useful for neuroinflammation (T1, T2, FLAIR, diffusion, gadolinium-enhanced imaging)
Imaging patterns characteristic of neuro-BD and their differential diagnoses
Role of MR venography and vascular imaging for venous thrombosis
Sensitivity limitations and reasons for normal MRI in early/aseptic meningitis
Advanced imaging techniques: PET, MR spectroscopy and their investigational roles
Imaging follow-up strategies in neuroinflammatory disorders

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Cerebrospinal Fluid Analysis: Interpretation in Infectious and Inflammatory Disorders
chapters.description: Guides interpretation of CSF findings in meningitis/encephalitis and sterile inflammatory conditions, including expected patterns for viral, bacterial, tuberculous, and autoimmune processes.
subtopics: CSF opening pressure, cell counts (neutrophilic vs lymphocytic), protein and glucose interpretation
Differentiating bacterial, viral, tuberculous and fungal meningitis by CSF profile
CSF testing modalities: culture, PCR, antigen tests, cytology and flow cytometry
CSF findings in autoimmune and neuroinflammatory diseases (e.g., neuro-BD, neurosarcoidosis)
Limitations of CSF testing and timing considerations for diagnostic yield
Utility of CSF cytokine measurements and investigational biomarkers

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Clinical Approach to Differential Diagnosis of Acute Aseptic Meningitis and Meningoencephalitis
chapters.description: Frameworks for evaluating patients with fever, headache and CSF pleocytosis, including infectious, autoimmune, neoplastic and other causes.
subtopics: History and examination clues to etiology: exposure, travel, immunosuppression, rash, mucosal lesions
Common infectious causes: HSV, VZV, enteroviruses, mycobacteria and fungal agents
Non-infectious causes: autoimmune encephalitis, vasculitis, drug reactions, systemic inflammatory diseases
When to start empiric antimicrobials/antivirals and choices of agents
Role of ancillary testing: imaging, serology, autoimmune panels
Stepwise diagnostic strategy and when to consider brain biopsy

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Laboratory Tests and Biomarkers Relevant to Systemic Inflammation and Differential Diagnoses
chapters.description: Overview of blood and specialized tests used in evaluating systemic inflammation, infectious screens and screening markers for conditions like sarcoidosis and hematologic malignancy.
subtopics: Acute phase reactants: CRP, ESR and interpretation in systemic inflammation
Markers used in sarcoidosis (ACE, lysozyme) and their sensitivity/specificity
Soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R) and its relevance to lymphoma and inflammation
Viral serologies and PCR testing for CNS pathogens (HSV, VZV, enterovirus)
Autoantibody panels used in systemic autoimmune disease screening
Interpretation of HLA-B51 testing and its role in BD evaluation

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Pharmacology of Colchicine and Other Therapies Used in Behçet's Disease
chapters.description: Mechanisms of action, therapeutic indications, dosing principles, adverse effects and important interactions of colchicine and a summary of other immunomodulatory agents used in BD (corticosteroids, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, TNF inhibitors).
subtopics: Colchicine: mechanism (microtubule inhibition, neutrophil function modulation), pharmacokinetics and dosing
Common and serious adverse effects of colchicine (gastrointestinal, neuromyopathy, cytopenias)
Drug interactions (CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors) and renal/hepatic dose adjustments
Role of corticosteroids in acute neuroinflammatory presentations: dosing and tapering strategies
Steroid-sparing immunosuppressants: azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide
Biologic agents (anti-TNF, interferon) — indications, monitoring and safety

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Rhabdomyolysis: Pathophysiology, Causes and Relationship to Electrolyte Disorders
chapters.description: Explores causes and mechanisms of muscle breakdown, diagnostic evaluation, complications (including acute kidney injury), and the association between severe hyponatraemia and rhabdomyolysis.
subtopics: Definition and pathophysiology of rhabdomyolysis; role of intracellular ion shifts and ATP depletion
Common causes: trauma, exertion, drugs, metabolic disturbances and electrolyte imbalances
Laboratory diagnosis: creatine kinase, myoglobinuria, electrolyte derangements
Complications: hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, acute tubular necrosis
Management: fluid resuscitation, monitoring, indications for renal replacement therapy
Mechanisms linking severe hyponatraemia to muscle injury

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Safety Principles in Empiric Antimicrobial and Antiviral Therapy for Suspected CNS Infections
chapters.description: Rationale for empiric therapy in suspected CNS infection, common empiric regimens, timing relative to diagnostics, and stewardship considerations.
subtopics: When to initiate empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and antivirals in suspected meningitis/encephalitis
Common empiric regimens for adults (e.g., cefepime/vancomycin/ampicillin, acyclovir) and indications for modification
Impact of prior antimicrobials on diagnostic yield and steps to mitigate
Duration of empiric therapy pending results and de-escalation principles
Adverse effects and interactions relevant to neurologic patients
Coordination with microbiology for targeted testing (PCR, cultures, antigen assays)

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Multidisciplinary Care, Monitoring and Rehabilitation in Multisystem Inflammatory Disease
chapters.description: Principles of coordinating care across specialties (neurology, rheumatology, infectious disease, endocrinology, dermatology and rehabilitation), monitoring for complications and long-term follow-up strategies.
subtopics: Roles of different specialties in evaluation and management of multisystem inflammatory disease
Monitoring for treatment response and adverse effects (laboratory and imaging follow-up)
Rehabilitation principles for functional decline after acute illness
Patient education, vaccination considerations and infection risk mitigation during immunosuppression
Long-term surveillance for disease recurrence and organ-specific complications
Psychosocial and quality-of-life considerations in chronic inflammatory disorders
